records.name: Florian Huber
records.bio: Huber authored an object-history study devoted to Blaschka sea-anemone models. The project uses it as a comparative secondary source for early model groups and their later collection histories.
records.open: A stable open web copy or authority record has not yet been linked.

records.name: Eleonora Weixelbaumer
records.bio: Weixelbaumer is named in the current Seitenstetten project as providing conservation-restoration support, including preparatory work on Blaschka sea-anemone models. Her role makes treatment planning part of the documented rediscovery process.

records.name: Isabella Gmeindl
records.bio: Gmeindl is named in the current Seitenstetten project as providing conservation-restoration support for the natural-history collections, including preparatory work on the rediscovered Blaschka sea-anemone models.

records.name: Julia D. Sigwart
records.bio: Sigwart’s study of the Dublin Blaschka Congress provides comparative collection context and includes an object-specific Oxford anchor: an Anthea cereus model acquired in 1867 and explicitly compared with its published zoological illustration source.

records.name: Adrian Norris
records.bio: Norris’s 1995 curatorial account is the central modern source for the Leeds Blaschka models. It records the historical acquisition of sixty-four sea-anemone models, twenty-seven extant examples in 1995, war and time damage, Armitage’s salvage and the Corning-led reidentification of the group.
records.open: The 1995 count must remain a dated survival checkpoint rather than a current total.

records.name: Susan M. Rossi-Wilcox
records.roles: museum historian · Blaschka workshop and collection research
records.bio: Rossi-Wilcox examined the Leeds material and recognized the rarity and significance of its very early models. Her broader research on the Blaschkas and their lampworking practice also makes her a major modern interpreter of workshop technique and surviving collections.

records.name: Sonia Wanson
records.bio: Wanson coordinated the Liège restoration, exhibition and catalogue project and co-authored Blaschka: Maîtres et modèles. Institutional accounts also preserve her explanation of the collection’s teaching rationale and post-restoration displayability.

records.name: Jacques Ninane
records.bio: Ninane co-authored the Liège collection catalogue and is credited for object photography in the modern presentation of the collection. His work forms part of the project’s visual and publication history after conservation.

records.name: Ruthanna Dyer
records.bio: Dyer studied the educational use of Blaschka marine models in North American post-secondary institutions using Ward papers and Blaschka business records. Her work is a key synthesis for connecting the dealer network to classroom and museum use.

records.name: Rüdiger Bieler
records.bio: Bieler’s history of the Field Museum molluscan collections reconstructs the Ward’s World’s Columbian Exposition material, including Blaschka glass models, the transfer into the museum and later photographic and display anchors.
